text:
maria: quick handover — I'm taking primary for the next 8h (APAC window). Current state: no active page, but we've been seeing intermittent 503s from model-cache-us-west over the last 45m. Low customer impact so far (few requests retried).

incident-bot: [ALERT SUMMARY] 503 spike on /v1/generate served by model-cache-us-west; window 2026-03-15T01:00Z -> ongoing; p95 token latency bumped to 780ms; error-rate ~1.8%. Incident severity: S2 (customer degraded).

maria: runbook pointers below — keep this thread for on-call notes and updates. Important quick checks: curl health, check node restart jitter, check KV eviction logs.

sam: I'm secondary for the same window (18:00-02:00 UTC). I can jump on pages if noise > 2x baseline.

lee: Heads up — there is a known maintenance window tomorrow in eu-central which will reduce cross-region capacity. Could make fallback slower; watch routing policy.

maria: coverage gaps: after 02:00 UTC we only have one infra engineer on rotation (dan). If pages go noisy overnight, please escalate to the SRE rotation per the runbook.

dan: noted. I'll be available for escalation 02:00-10:00 UTC. If you need me earlier ping directly. For paging rules: if > 3 consecutive pages in 15m, escalate to infra@redwood.com and DM me.

maria: quick triage checklist (do these in order):
1) Confirm error rate and scope: 
   - kubectl logs -n inference deployment/model-cache --since=30m | grep "503"
2) Health endpoints: 
   - curl -sS https://model-cache-us-west.health/internal/health | jq .status
3) Check KV eviction spike: 
   - gcloud logging read "resource.labels.cluster_name=\"model-cache-us-west\" AND textPayload:\"evict\"" --limit 50
4) If cache nodes unhealthy -> run rolling restart for the pool (see step below).

maria: rolling restart (only if nodes fail healthcheck):
```
# scale down + back up, small step to avoid thundering herd
kubectl scale deployment model-cache --replicas=3 -n inference
sleep 30
kubectl rollout restart deployment/model-cache -n inference
```

ops-bot: runbook pinned: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/model-cache-throttle. Also quick KB: https://internal.redwood/ops/playbooks/cache-eviction-cheats

sam: if you need to fallback routes, toggle policy: `redwoodctl routing set --policy=regional-fallback --dry-run` first. If dry-run looks ok, remove --dry-run.

maria: customer impact note to paste into status page if needed: "Some customers may see intermittent 503s and increased latency for model generation in us-west. We are investigating and applying mitigation steps — retries recommended. No data loss reported."

lee: FYI if you want temporary mitigation without restart: reduce per-connection concurrency on the cache layer: `kubectl set env deployment/model-cache MAX_CONN=200 -n inference` — that lowers immediate pressure but might increase latencies; use with caution.

maria: update 18:32Z — observed small recovery after cache eviction TTL bump. Error-rate down to 0.9% last 10m. Leaving primary on until metric stable for 30m.

incident-bot: [METRICS SNAPSHOT] p50=120ms p95=650ms p99=1.4s error-rate=0.9% requests=48k/10m

sam: acknowledged. I'll monitor dashboards + keep this thread as the source of truth. If anything changes I'll call the bridge. :phone_off_hook:

dan: if the restart path is needed, prefer staged restart: drain one node at a time and check cache hit-rate between steps. Link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/rolling-restart-guidelines

maria: final note for whoever picks up after me: primary = maria, secondary = sam, escalation = dan (infra). Runbooks pinned in thread. If you take over, post "taken" and time.

sam: taken — 19:10Z. monitoring. :white_check_mark:

maria: thanks team — posting handoff summary to handoff channel after this.

ops-bot: reminder: attach runbook links to the incident ticket and mark coverage in PagerDuty.

lee: ping if you want me to pre-warm extra replicas before eu maintenance window.

sam: will do if we see any regression.

maria: end of thread for now — last check 19:45Z p95 back to 420ms, error-rate steady 0.6%. If it slips back, reopen thread. :thumbsup:
